others.route: Permit to enter and reside, or written permission to work (Principal Immigration Officer)

note: Tonga: a visitor's permit lets a visitor stay up to six months on condition that he takes up no employment without the Principal Immigration Officer's written permission, and a permit to enter and reside is issued on conditions as to the profession or occupation its holder may engage in and who may employ him (Immigration Act, Cap. 62, 1988 Revised Edition, ss. 9–10). The Immigration (Amendment) Acts of 1989, 1996, 1998 and 2001, read too, change neither condition (1998 adds multiple-entry visas and extensions past six months). Read in PacLII's copies through archive.org (the Act's snapshot of 17 December 2024, the amendments' of 2011), since PacLII and Tonga's own legislation site refuse this client; Tonga's later revised editions weren't reachable, so a later change can't be ruled out. No performers' exemption and no days without the permission are named.

sources.title: Immigration Act (Tonga, Cap. 62, 1988 Revised Edition), ss. 9–10 (PacLII's copy, archive.org snapshot of 17 December 2024)
sources.said: The Principal Immigration Officer may issue a permit in the prescribed form to any person applying to enter and reside in the Kingdom, upon such conditions as to the security to be furnished, the profession or occupation which the holder may exercise or engage in and the person by whom the holder may be employed within Tonga ... shall not take up employment in the Kingdom without the permission in writing of the Principal Immigration Officer

sources.title: Immigration (Amendment) Act 1998 (Tonga) (PacLII's copy, archive.org snapshot of 13 March 2011)
sources.said: Section 9(2) of the Principal Act is amended by deleting the words "such written".
